iPIXELcolorHA

A Home Assistant integration for iPixel Bluetooth LED matrix panels (the ones that advertise as LED_BLE_… and are normally used with the iPixel Color phone app). From Home Assistant you can:

  • show scrolling or still text in any colour,
  • show pictures and animated GIFs,
  • draw graphs of your sensor data (bars, lines or dots),
  • fill the panel with random flashing pixels,
  • colour single pixels or rectangles live, for status dots and progress bars,
  • show pictures and graphs as live frames that are not saved,
  • switch to the panel's built-in clock,
  • turn the panel on and off, set its brightness and flip it upside down.

It talks to the panel through Home Assistant's own Bluetooth, so it works with the Bluetooth adapter in your Home Assistant machine or through an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy.

Requirements

  • Home Assistant 2026.10 or newer.
  • Bluetooth that can reach the panel: either a Bluetooth adapter in the Home Assistant machine, or an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy with active: true (see A Bluetooth proxy for the panel).
  • An iPixel panel 16 or 32 pixels high. Tested on 192 x 32 panels (panel type 143). Other widths are recognised during setup; panels of other heights (such as 64 x 64) are not supported yet.

One connection at a time. The panel accepts a single Bluetooth connection. While Home Assistant is connected, the iPixel Color phone app cannot reach the panel (see Keep connected), and only one integration can use it, so remove or disable any other integration for the same panel, such as iPIXEL Color.

Install

  1. Copy the iPIXELcolorHA folder to /config/custom_components/iPIXELcolorHA on your Home Assistant machine (for example with the Samba share or File editor app).
  2. Restart Home Assistant.
  3. Go to Settings → Devices & services. Your panel should appear under Discovered as LED_BLE_…; choose Add. If it doesn't, choose Add integration → iPIXELcolorHA and pick it from the list.
  4. Setup connects to the panel and reads its size. Check the height and width it shows (for example 32 and 192) and choose Submit.

Each panel is added on its own, so repeat step 3 for every panel you have.

Your first message

  1. Open Settings → Devices & services → iPIXELcolorHA and select your panel.
  2. Type some text into the Message box and press Enter. After a second or two it scrolls across the panel in white.
  3. Now try an action with your own colour. Go to Tools → Actions (called Developer Tools before Home Assistant 2026.8), choose iPIXELcolorHA: Display text, pick your panel's Message entity as the target, fill in a message and a colour, and choose Perform action.

The same action in YAML, for scripts and automations:

action: ipixelcolorha.display_text
target:
  entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
data:
  message: "Dinner is ready"
  color: [255, 160, 0]

Finding your entity ID: every panel gets entities named after it, such as text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message, where a1b2c3d4 is the end of the name the panel advertises (LED_BLE_A1B2C3D4). All actions below target this Message entity; replace the ID in the examples with yours.

Colours are written as [red, green, blue], each from 0 to 255, for example [255, 0, 0] for red. In the action form you can use the colour picker instead.

Entities

Each panel has these entities:

Entity Example ID What it does
Message text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message Type text to show it with the default colour, speed and animation from the options. Also the target for every action.
Panel light.led_ble_a1b2c3d4 Turns the panel's LEDs on and off and sets their brightness.
Upside down switch.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_upside_down Rotates everything by 180 degrees, for panels mounted the other way up.
Sync time button.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_sync_time Sets the panel's clock to Home Assistant's time.

The panel doesn't report anything back, so these entities show the last value set from Home Assistant, not what the panel is actually showing. If you change something with the phone app, Home Assistant won't know.

The panel's firmware versions are read the first time Home Assistant connects to it and shown on its device page (Settings → Devices & services → iPIXELcolorHA → the panel): Firmware is the main chip (MCU) version and Hardware the Bluetooth module's, as the phone app shows them under device info. With Keep connected on they are read when Home Assistant starts; otherwise on the first send.

Actions

Action Shows
ipixelcolorha.display_text Text, still or scrolling
ipixelcolorha.display_image A picture or animated GIF
ipixelcolorha.display_graph A bar, line or dot graph of numbers
ipixelcolorha.display_random_pixels Flashing random-colour pixels or squares
ipixelcolorha.show_clock The panel's built-in clock
ipixelcolorha.countdown The panel's built-in countdown timer
ipixelcolorha.stopwatch The panel's built-in stopwatch
ipixelcolorha.draw_pixels Single pixels or filled rectangles, live
ipixelcolorha.draw_frame Several colours of rectangles, pixels and text as one picture
ipixelcolorha.delete_slots, ipixelcolorha.delete_all Nothing: they clear saved programs

Every field except the ones marked required can be left out. Values not given come from the panel's options.

Display text

Field Values Default
message (required) The text to show
color [R, G, B] Text colour from the options (white)
background_color [R, G, B] Black
speed 0 (slowest) to 100 80
effect 0 still, 1 scroll left, 2 scroll right, 5 blink, 6 breathe, 7 snowflakes 1
rainbow_mode 0 or 1 off (solid colour), 2 to 9 rainbow presets 0
save_slot 1 to 10, see save slots 1

Text that fits the panel can be shown still (effect: 0); longer text should scroll. On a 192-pixel-wide panel about 10 characters fit.

action: ipixelcolorha.display_text
target:
  entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
data:
  message: "Washing done"
  color: [0, 255, 0]
  effect: 0

Display image

Shows a picture or an animated GIF, resized to the panel. Give exactly one of file or url.

Field Values Default
file A file on the Home Assistant machine, in /config/www or a folder listed in allowlist_external_dirs
url A web address of a picture, up to 10 MB
resize fit (whole picture, gaps filled), crop (fills the panel, edges cut off), stretch (fills the panel, shape distorted) fit
background_color [R, G, B] for the gaps left by fit Black
hide_loading true or false, see hide loading false
save_slot 1 to 10 1
live true shows it at once as a live frame instead of saving it, see live frames false

PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP work. Animated GIF, PNG and WebP files stay animated and keep each frame's timing.

action: ipixelcolorha.display_image
target:
  entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
data:
  file: /config/www/matrix/logo.gif
  resize: crop

Display graph

Draws numbers as a graph that fills the panel, with an optional label in a strip along the top. Give exactly one of values, points or series.

Field Values Default
values A list of numbers, drawn evenly spaced, oldest on the left, up to 1024
points A list of [x, y] pairs, up to 1024
series Up to 8 sets of points, each with its own color (see the example)
style bar, line or dots bar for values, line for points and series
color [R, G, B] Text colour from the options
background_color [R, G, B] Black
x_min, x_max The x values at the left and right edges (not for bars) The data's own range
y_min, y_max The y values at the bottom and top (bars always start at 0) The data's own range
label Short text shown above the graph None
hide_loading true or false false
save_slot 1 to 10 1
live true shows it at once as a live frame instead of saving it, see live frames false

Points outside the range are drawn at its edge. Lines are 1 pixel wide, and a dim zero line is drawn when the y range crosses zero. maximum still works as an older name for y_max.

A bar graph of a list of numbers:

action: ipixelcolorha.display_graph
target:
  entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
data:
  values: [0, 2, 5, 7, 7, 4, 0, 1, 3]
  color: [255, 170, 0]
  label: "Rain mm"

A line graph of x-y points, with the y axis starting at 0:

action: ipixelcolorha.display_graph
target:
  entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
data:
  points: [[0, 1.2], [15, 3.4], [20, 3.1], [60, 2.0]]
  y_min: 0
  label: "Power kW"

Two lines in different colours, with a fixed x range of 0 to 24 hours:

action: ipixelcolorha.display_graph
target:
  entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
data:
  series:
    - points: [[0, 18.5], [6, 17.9], [12, 21.0], [18, 19.2]]
      color: [255, 80, 0]
    - points: [[0, 8.0], [6, 6.5], [12, 14.0], [18, 10.1]]
      color: [0, 160, 255]
  x_min: 0
  x_max: 24

To graph a sensor, build the list with a template. For example, if an input_text helper holds a string of single digits:

data:
  values: "{{ states('input_text.power_history') | list | map('int', 0) | list }}"

Display random pixels

Fills the panel with bright random colours that change at every step of a looping animation.

Field Values Default
steps 1 to 50 different random pictures 10
duration 20 to 10000 milliseconds per picture 200
colors 2 to 256 colours, spread evenly round the colour wheel 4
block_size 1 to 32: each colour fills a square this many pixels wide (1 is single pixels, 2 is 2 x 2 squares, and so on) 1
hide_loading true or false false
save_slot 1 to 10 1 
action: ipixelcolorha.display_random_pixels
target:
  entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
data:
  steps: 10
  duration: 200
  block_size: 4
  hide_loading: true

Random pictures are large, so they take a while to send. Fewer colours and bigger blocks make them smaller. For 10 steps on a 192 x 32 panel:

Colours Block size Size Time via ESP32-C3 proxy Time via ESP32-S3 proxy
2 1 11 KB about 11 s about 3 s
4 1 20 KB about 20 s about 5 s
4 4 10 KB about 10 s about 3 s
16 1 40 KB about 41 s about 10 s

Times were measured for some rows and estimated from the measured speed (about 1 KB/s and 4 KB/s) for the rest.

Draw pixels

Colours single pixels using the panel's drawing mode (the phone app's DIY screen). Only the changed pixels are sent, a few bytes each, so the panel updates almost at once instead of waiting for a whole picture. Useful for status dots, progress bars and small indicators.

Field Values Default
points A list of [x, y] pixels. x runs from 0 at the left to width - 1, y from 0 at the top to height - 1 None
rectangles A list of filled rectangles as [x1, y1, x2, y2] corners, both included None
color [R, G, B]; [0, 0, 0] turns pixels off Text colour from the options
clear true clears the whole panel first; false draws over what is shown false

A red dot in the top-right corner of a 192 x 32 panel, over whatever is showing:

action: ipixelcolorha.draw_pixels
target:
  entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
data:
  points: [[190, 0], [191, 0], [190, 1], [191, 1]]
  color: [255, 0, 0]

A progress bar along the bottom two rows, filled to a percentage. Send it twice: once in dim grey for the empty bar, then in green for the filled part:

sequence:
  - action: ipixelcolorha.draw_pixels
    target:
      entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
    data:
      clear: true
      rectangles: [[0, 30, 191, 31]]
      color: [20, 20, 20]
  - action: ipixelcolorha.draw_pixels
    target:
      entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
    data:
      rectangles: "{{ [[0, 30, (states('sensor.washer_progress') | int(0) * 191 // 100), 31]] }}"
      color: [0, 255, 0]

The drawing is not saved: sending text, a picture or the clock afterwards replaces it.

Draw frame

Paints several coloured layers (filled rectangles, single pixels and text) into one picture and sends it in a single go, so the panel changes from the old picture to the new one at once. Use it instead of several draw_pixels calls when a display needs more than one colour: those draw each colour separately, bit by bit, and clear blanks the panel first.

Field Values Default
layers (required) A list of up to 32 layers, painted in order (later ones on top). Each has color [R, G, B] (required) and any of: rectangles (filled [x1, y1, x2, y2] corners, both included), points ([x, y] pixels), text with x, y, size (pixels, default half the height) and anchor None
background_color [R, G, B] behind the layers [0, 0, 0]
save_slot Slot 1 to 10 the picture is saved to Save slot from the options
hide_loading true keeps the old picture showing while the new one is sent, instead of the panel's loading screen true
live true sends it as a live frame instead of saving it false

Coordinates are as for draw pixels: x from 0 at the left, y from 0 at the top. anchor says which point of the text sits at (x, y): l, m or r (left, middle, right) then a, m or s (top, middle, baseline), for example rm for right-aligned and centred vertically. Text uses the bundled font without anti-aliasing.

A progress bar with the percentage beside it, on a 192 x 32 panel:

action: ipixelcolorha.draw_frame
target:
  entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
data:
  layers:
    - color: [30, 30, 30]
      rectangles: [[0, 8, 143, 23]]
    - color: [0, 255, 0]
      rectangles: "{{ [[0, 8, [states('sensor.washer_progress') | int(0) * 143 // 100, 1] | max, 23]] }}"
    - color: [255, 255, 255]
      text: "{{ states('sensor.washer_progress') }}%"
      x: 191
      y: 16
      anchor: rm

Live frames

display_image and display_graph normally save what they send in a slot (see save slots). With live: true the picture is sent the way the phone app's camera mode sends video: as a single JPEG frame that is shown straight away and not saved. Use it for pictures that change often, such as a graph refreshed every few minutes, so the panel's memory is not rewritten each time. Animations are not played live: only their first frame is shown.

action: ipixelcolorha.display_graph
target:
  entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
data:
  values: "{{ states('input_text.power_history') | list | map('int', 0) | list }}"
  style: line
  live: true

action: ipixelcolorha.display_image
target:
  entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
data:
  url: "http://homeassistant.local:8123/local/camera_snapshot.jpg"
  resize: crop
  live: true

Because nothing is saved, a live frame is expected to be lost when the panel loses power; it then goes back to its saved program.

Show clock

Sets the panel's clock to Home Assistant's time and switches to the panel's built-in clock.

Field Values Default
style (required) 1 to 9, the clock designs from the phone app 1
use_24h true or false true
show_date true or false true 
action: ipixelcolorha.show_clock
target:
  entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
data:
  style: 2

Countdown

Runs the panel's own countdown timer, which counts down on the panel by itself. These timer commands come from iPixel Color 3.8; older panel firmware ignores them. Panels with firmware 29.12 (Bluetooth 1.22) run the stopwatch but don't answer the countdown command, so nothing changes on them. The firmware version is on the panel's device page (see Entities).

Field Values Default
command (required) start, pause, resume or reset start
minutes 0 to 90 0
seconds 0 to 59 0

start needs a time above 0:00. Like the app, send the remaining time with pause and resume too if you know it; reset clears the timer to 0:00.

action: ipixelcolorha.countdown
target:
  entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
data:
  command: start
  minutes: 5

Stopwatch

Runs the panel's own stopwatch, counting up from zero on the panel. Like the countdown, it needs panel firmware that has it; firmware 29.12 does.

Field Values Default
command (required) start, pause, resume or reset start 
action: ipixelcolorha.stopwatch
target:
  entity_id: text.led_ble_a1b2c3d4_message
data:
  command: start

Hide loading

While a picture, graph or random-pixel animation is being sent, the panel plays its own loading animation. Add hide_loading: true to those actions to dim the panel to brightness 0 during the upload and then put the brightness back (to the last value set on the Panel light), so the panel stays dark until the new picture appears.

Save slots

The panel stores what you send in one of 10 numbered program slots. Every action writes to slot 1 unless you give a different save_slot (or change the default in the options), so each new message replaces the last one.

  • ipixelcolorha.delete_slots with slots: [2, 3] clears the given slots.
  • ipixelcolorha.delete_all clears every slot, including anything saved from the phone app. It can't be undone.

Options

Open Settings → Devices & services → iPIXELcolorHA, select the panel and choose Configure (the cog).

Option What it does Default
Height, Width The panel's size in pixels. Filled in during setup. Read from the panel
Connect via Which Bluetooth adapter or proxy to use. See below. Automatic
Keep connected Keeps the Bluetooth connection open between sends. See below. On
Disconnect when idle Closes a kept connection after this many minutes with nothing sent; 0 never closes it. 0
Font file An optional TrueType font for text, for example /config/fonts/MyFont.ttf Built-in font
Text colour, Speed, Animation, Rainbow mode, Save slot The defaults used by the Message entity and by actions that leave these fields out White, 80, Scroll left, Off, 1

Connect via

Automatic lets Home Assistant use whichever adapter hears the panel best. If you have a Bluetooth proxy next to the panel, choose it here so Home Assistant always uses it. The list only shows adapters that can currently hear the panel.

Keep connected

With Keep connected on, Home Assistant connects on the first send and stays connected, so later commands go out straight away and the panel shows its Bluetooth icon only once. While connected:

  • the iPixel Color phone app can't reach the panel, and
  • an ESPHome proxy has one of its connection slots in use.

If you use the phone app sometimes, turn Keep connected off, or set Disconnect when idle to a few minutes. A dropped connection is reopened on the next send.

A Bluetooth proxy for the panel

If your Home Assistant machine is far from the panel, an ESP32 board running ESPHome makes a good Bluetooth proxy. ESP32-S3 boards (such as the M5Stack Atom S3 Lite) send about four times faster than ESP32-C3 boards. A minimal configuration:

esphome:
  name: matrix-ble-proxy

esp32:
  board: m5stack-atoms3
  framework:
    type: esp-idf

wifi:
  ssid: !secret wifi_ssid
  password: !secret wifi_password

api:
  encryption:
    key: !secret api_key

ota:
  - platform: esphome

esp32_ble_tracker:
  scan_parameters:
    active: true

bluetooth_proxy:
  active: true

Don't add an ESPHome ble_client for the panel: it would take the panel's only connection and lock Home Assistant out.

Troubleshooting

"The Bluetooth adapter or proxy … cannot currently see the LED matrix" The adapter chosen in Connect via hasn't heard the panel recently. Usual causes:

  • Something else is still connected to the panel, so it isn't advertising. This often happens for a minute or so after Home Assistant restarts, or when the phone app is open. Wait, close the app, or switch the panel off and on at the plug.
  • The proxy is offline or too far away. Check it in Settings → Devices & services → ESPHome, or set Connect via to Automatic.

The panel plays its own animation while a picture is loading. That's the panel's firmware. Add hide_loading: true to the action.

Pictures and animations take a long time to arrive. Bluetooth to these panels is slow: from about 1 KB per second through an ESP32-C3 proxy to about 4 KB per second through an ESP32-S3. Use smaller pictures, fewer colours or bigger blocks for random pixels, or a faster proxy.

What I sent disappears after a minute or two. Check for an automation that sends to the same panel on a timer: each send replaces what was there.

"Home Assistant is not allowed to read …" from display_image. Put the file in /config/www, or add its folder to allowlist_external_dirs.

Seeing what's happening. On the iPIXELcolorHA integration page, choose Enable debug logging, try again, then Disable debug logging to download the log. It shows each connection and every reply from the panel.

Limitations

  • Text has no smoothing: each pixel is fully on or off.
  • The panel doesn't report its state, so the entities show what Home Assistant last sent, not what's on the panel.
  • Not supported yet: playing saved slots as a playlist, split-screen layouts, the music visualiser and scoreboard modes.
  • draw_pixels uses whole pixels in one colour per call; the app's mirror, move and erase drawing tools are not offered.
  • The phone app's up, down and laser text animations are not offered: the panel blocks them for horizontal text.
  • Rainbow modes 2 to 9 are presets in the panel's firmware, so how they look depends on the panel.

Developer notes

  • The protocol was traced from the iPixel Color 2.9.1 Android app. Each send writes frames to characteristic 0xFA02 in MTU-sized pieces and waits for the panel's acknowledgement on 0xFA03.
  • protocol.py has no Home Assistant imports. Its text encoding is checked byte for byte against this repository's commands.send_text. Run the tests from the repository root with python -m unittest discover -s tests/ipixelcolorha.
  • The Documentation link on the integration's page opens README.html, which the integration serves from Home Assistant itself at /ipixelcolorha/README.html (no internet needed). It is built from this file: after editing README.md, run python tools/build_ipixelcolorha_readme.py from the repository root (needs the markdown package). A test fails if README.html is out of date.
Served by the iPIXELcolorHA integration from its own README.md.
